idiom_name: struct implementing the trait with RefCell<Vec<Call>> as the journal
implementation_notes: Rust has no reflection for working implementations, so the fake is a hand-written type implementing the same trait; because trait methods take &self, both the store and the journal need interior mutability - RefCell in single-threaded tests, Mutex or RwLock when the fake must be Send/Sync - and Vec<Call> is the natural journal, since nothing in the standard library replaces this compound. mockall generates mocks with expectations, argument matchers and call counts (with(), times(), Sequence) but no behaviour, so it serves the mock row. Keep the fake behind the same trait the production code takes, expose the journal through an inherent test-only method, and place a shared fake in a test-support module rather than behind #[cfg(test)] so integration tests in tests/ (a separate crate) can use it too.
pitfalls: Holding a RefCell borrow across a call that re-enters the fake panics at runtime (already borrowed) - scope borrows tightly or use a Mutex.
A fake behind #[cfg(test)] is invisible to integration tests in tests/, which form a separate crate - put shared fakes in a test-support module.
Cloning the journal on every read is fine for a handful of calls but O(n) per assertion; expose an iterator or a predicate-filtered view for larger traces.
